    'Wisconsin': 117667,
    'Wyoming': 7638
}

# Sort by value descending and assign rank
sorted_values = sorted(states_data.values(), reverse=True)
print(f"Number of states: {len(sorted_values)}")
print(f"\nValues sorted descending (first 10):")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values[:10], 1):
    print(f"  Rank {i}: {v}")

# Calculate Zipf exponent using linear regression on log-log scale
# log(rank) = -s * log(value) + c
# So we regress log(rank) on log(value)
# The slope (with negative sign) is the Zipf exponent

log_ranks = []
log_values = []

for rank, value in enumerate(sorted_values, 1):
    log_ranks.append(math.log(rank))
    log_values.append(math.log(value))

# Linear regression: log(rank) = a + b * log(value)
# We want to find s where log(rank) = -s * log(value) + c
# So b = -s, and s = -b

n = len(sorted_values)
sum_x = sum(log_values)
sum_y = sum(log_ranks)
sum_xy = sum(log_values[i] * log_ranks[i] for i in range(n))
sum_x2 = sum(x * x for x in log_values)

# Calculate slope (b) and intercept (a)
b = (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x)
a = (sum_y - b * sum_x) / n

# Zipf exponent s = -b
s = -b

print(f"\nLinear regression results:")
print(f"  Slope (b): {b:.6f}")
print(f"  Intercept (a): {a:.6f}")
print(f"  Zipf exponent (s): {s:.6f}")
print(f"\nRounded to nearest thousandth: {round(s, 3)}")

# Also verify with Python's statistics
print(f"\nVerification - sorted values:")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values[:5], 1):
    print(f"  Rank {i}: log(rank)={math.log(i):.4f}, log(value)={math.log(v):.4f}")
